I fixed one bug in `src/wrap.py`, but I haven't run the tests since the edit. The shell was denied partway through, so the new test is unverified.

Your request didn't say what was broken, and the existing 5 tests passed. I read `wrap()` and found this: when the first word is longer than `width`, it appended an empty string as a line. `wrap("abcdef gh", 3)` returned `["", "abcdef", "gh"]`. The fix is an `if cur:` guard before the append. The same case also hit a long word at the start of the text.

I added `test_wrap_long_first_word_no_empty_line` in `tests/test_wrap.py`. It expects `["abcdef", "gh"]`. To check, run `python -m pytest -q` in the repo, or let me retry the shell.

If the problem you saw is something else, tell me what you ran and what you got. A word longer than `width` still gets its own line unsplit. I left that alone because it may be intended.
